self_assessment.text:
Texas Hold'em is a popular poker variant where players aim to make the best five-card hand using a combination of their two hole cards and five community cards. The game involves betting rounds after each stage of the hand, with the goal of winning the pot containing all the bets placed.

In Texas Hold'em, players receive two private cards, known as hole cards, face down. Then, five community cards are dealt face up in the center of the table in three stages: the flop, the turn, and the river. Players can use any combination of their hole cards and the community cards to form their best five-card hand.

The betting rounds occur after each stage of the hand, starting with the player to the left of the dealer button. Players can choose to call, raise, or fold their hand. The player with the best five-card hand at the end of the hand wins the pot.

Texas Hold'em is a game of skill and chance, requiring both strategic thinking and a bit of luck. Understanding hand rankings, betting patterns, and opponent behavior are crucial for success in this exciting poker variant.
